summary: Today’s pulse tracks Trump says truce ‘over’ as Iran reports US attack near nuclear plant – Middle East crisis live, Ukraine strikes Russian ships near Crimea, escalating attacks on fuel supplies, and Factory fire kills at least 28 in China's 'shoe capital'. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are attacks, strikes, and attack. In the background, Former Olympian pleads not guilty in Washington reflecting pool damage case after Trump alleged vandalism – live and Farage launches preemptive attack on Commons standards committee, claiming it won’t judge him fairly – UK politics live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Trump says truce ‘over’ as Iran reports US attack near nuclear plant – Middle East crisis live
headlines.description: Sides exchange strikes with Iranian media saying attacks reported near facility in Bushehr Kuwait’s foreign ministry has issued a statement condemning the Iranian attacks against the country. It reads almost identical to the statement issued yesterday, although emphasises Kuwait’s sovereignty is “a red line” . “The state of Kuwait reserves its full rights to take all necessary measures to protect its security and preserve its sovereignty,” it said.

headlines.title: Ukraine strikes Russian ships near Crimea, escalating attacks on fuel supplies
headlines.description: The attacks appear to be the latest phase of Ukraine's bid to choke off supplies and routes into and out of occupied Crimea.

headlines.title: Factory fire kills at least 28 in China's 'shoe capital'
headlines.description: Footage shows huge flames rising from a building and thick, black smoke rising into the sky.

headlines.title: Former Olympian pleads not guilty in Washington reflecting pool damage case after Trump alleged vandalism – live
headlines.description: David Hearn was charged with a single felony count of property destruction last week Hearn, 67, from Maryland, was arrested last month after stopping by the pool on a bike ride. He told several outlets that he was detained for almost five hours after he reached into the water to inspect what he described a piece of the blue liner that was partially detached from the bottom of the pool as he was curious what it felt like.

headlines.title: Farage launches preemptive attack on Commons standards committee, claiming it won’t judge him fairly – UK politics live
headlines.description: Reform UK leader also tells the Daily Mail he did not anticipate main parties would not stand candidates in Clacton byelection Reform activists urged to switch focus from Manchester to Farage’s Clacton contest The untold story of why Reform figures face NCA scrutiny Andy Burnham has posted a video on social media confirming that he has nominated himself for Labour leader. Nominations opened this morning. Labour will publish daily updates on how many nominations he has received (it’s an open process, and so names of MPs nominating a candidate are published), and Burnham says we should get the first update at about 7pm tonight. Al Carns , the former defence minister, has not been in to nominate himself. Last night he confirmed what everyone else already knew – that he would not be standing as a candidate. He said : I’d hoped a leadership contest would give us the opportunity for a proper debate. But months of internal Labour politics isn’t what the country needs right now. We’ve got to get on with the job. @AndyBurnham’s earned this and he’s got my full backing.

headlines.title: ‘It was back-to-back explosions’: Iranians recall 48 hours of terror after US attack on port cities
headlines.description: Residents in Bandar Abbas and Sirik regions describe communities in fear and ‘feeling abandoned’ after US launch fresh strikes over two-day period Residents in southern Iran have described two nights of fear this week after explosions shook coastal communities as the US launched fresh strikes on targets including the port cities of Bandar Abbas and Sirik . US Central Command confirmed the attacks, saying they were carried out to “further degrade their ability to threaten freedom of navigation in the strait of Hormuz”.

headlinePool.title: Former top BHP economist urges tougher government policies to push miners to decarbonise
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: ‘The preferred policy is, of course, a carbon price,’ Dr Huw McKay says, amid slowdown in BHP action on emissions Internal documents, leaked to Guardian Australia and the ABC earlier this year, showed BHP had delayed vast renewables projects in the Pilbara, scrapped a project that would have delivered significant cuts to global emissions, and war-gamed options to push the electrification of its polluting diesel truck and train fleets into the next two decades.

headlinePool.title: Growing legal bill for failed defence of controversial NSW protest laws runs to hundreds of thousands of dollars
headlinePool.description: Exclusive : Documents show $117,455.50 was spent in a single legal fight over laws rushed through after Bondi attack The costs, outlined in documents obtained by Guardian Australia via freedom of information legislation, include $117,455.50 of taxpayers’ money on a single challenge to controversial public assembly restriction declaration (Pard) laws. Those laws were enacted following the Bondi beach terror attack and were in place during a now infamous rally against the Israeli president , Isaac Herzog, in February.

headlinePool.title: This huge hairy-legged Australian arachnid may be the fastest spider on the planet
headlinePool.description: A brown huntsman is the quickest of more than 250 species analysed by scientists in the UK and Germany If arachnophobes were not frightened enough by the horrific ability of Australia’s huntsman spiders to drag dead mice up the sides of fridges , they now have another reason. They might be the fastest spiders on the planet.

headlinePool.title: Former Olympian pleads not guilty in reflecting pool vandalism charges
headlinePool.description: Canoeist David Hearn plead not guilty in D.C. Superior Court Thursday to a charge of destruction of property causing more than $1,000 in damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

headlinePool.title: Former US Olympian pleads not guilty to damaging reflecting pool amid Trump’s renovation
headlinePool.description: David Hearn is accused of destroying ‘American flag blue’ lining material on the bottom of the reflecting pool David Hearn, a former Olympic canoe racer, pleaded not guilty on Thursday to damaging Washington’s reflecting pool after a $14.7m renovation project. Hearn, a three-time US Olympian, was indicted last week on a single felony count of property destruction. He appeared in local superior court in Washington DC, to enter the plea after he was criminally charged over the incident in mid-June.

headlinePool.title: Doreen Lawrence will not foot any of legal bill for failed attempt to sue Daily Mail
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Source close to co-claimant Prince Harry says he is protective of social campaigner and will not ‘see her out of pocket’ Doreen Lawrence, the social justice campaigner, will not foot any of a multimillion-pound bill for the failed attempt to sue the publisher of the Daily Mail, the Guardian understands. Lawrence, the mother of the murdered teenager Stephen Lawrence , whose case was the subject of a long-running Daily Mail campaign from the late 1990s, was one of seven claimants defeated in court over claims the Mail titles used unlawful methods to source stories.

headlinePool.title: Conspiracies and regrets abound in Dune: Part Three trailer
headlinePool.description: "You promised me that you would never take power in your name."

headlinePool.title: Sharp drop in ships crossing Strait of Hormuz after US and Iran trade strikes
headlinePool.description: Data shows a decline in the number of ships - many carrying oil and gas - going through the waterway after attacks this week.

headlinePool.title: Democrat Graham Platner suspends campaign for key US Senate race after assault allegation
headlinePool.description: The decision came days after a woman accused him of sexual assault, an accusation he says is "categorically false".
